subject: Post-call: Discovery recap & POC charter (Vectra Health)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Ruiz <aruiz@vectrahealth.com>, David Chen <dchen@vectrahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Discovery recap & POC charter (Vectra Health)

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Below is a short recap, proposed POC scope, owners, and immediate access asks so we can get the kickoff scheduled. If anything below is off, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points we heard
- Production extraction pipelines are inconsistent: high variance in latency (spikes up to 1.2s p95) and frequent fallbacks to batch jobs.
- Token costs are unpredictable during peak batch runs (billing spikes).
- Regulatory needs: PII redaction and strict auditability for PHI-bearing documents.

Primary goals for the POC
1) Validate we can meet a 200ms p95 for the common extraction flow (typical request length ~1.5k tokens) under a production-like workload.
2) Demonstrate a 2.5–3x reduction in per-token inference cost via batching + KV caching/quantization without degrading extraction F1 by >2 points.
3) Verify access controls & audit logs meet your compliance requirements for HIPAA-adjacent workflows.

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks)
- Workload: run two evaluation workloads — (A) production-sampled extraction stream (approx 1M tokens/day simulated), (B) a 10% subset of long-context, 8k+ token documents for stress.
- Deliverables: performance summary (latency percentiles, throughput), cost analysis (tokens, infer ops), quality evals (extraction precision/recall on labeled set), and ops runbook for failovers.
- Tech approach: use Redwood hosted sandbox with dedicated pool, prefix caching for common prompts, and a quantized model variant for cost runs.

Owners & roles
- Vectra: Alexandra Ruiz — Product lead (success criteria, sample sets), David Chen — Engineering (access, infra).
- Redwood: Karthik Iyer — Sales lead (scheduling, commercial), Ben Carter — Customer Success (onboarding & eval facilitation), Monica Patel — Solutions/Infra (sandbox provisioning, network setup).

Timeline (proposed)
- Access & dataset delivery: by Thu 8/26
- Sandbox provisioning & baseline run: Fri 8/27
- Quality + cost runs: week of 8/30
- Wrap & decision readout: Fri 9/10

Immediate asks (what we need to start)
- Shared sample set: 2k labeled documents (or a 10k-row CSV with representative rows) and schema.
- Network: IP allowlist or VPC peering info for our sandbox (see Monica’s note below for specifics).
- Compliance: example redaction rules and any required retention policies.

Attachments included: vectra-poc-charter-v0.1.pdf, vectra-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (mutual action plan with milestones).

Next step: can we confirm a kickoff window next Monday 8/30 or Tuesday 8/31? I’ll lock in calendar once we confirm.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Post-call: Discovery recap & POC charter (Vectra Health)

Thanks Karthik — useful summary. A few clarifications / tech asks from our side: 

> On Mon, 23 Aug 2026 at 15:02, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> > Immediate asks (what we need to start)
> > - Shared sample set: 2k labeled documents (or a 10k-row CSV with representative rows) and schema.

1) We can provide a 5k-row CSV and a small labeled extraction set (~800 examples). I’ll get that uploaded. Is CSV fine or do you prefer newline-delimited JSON?
2) Network: we prefer VPC peering but can do IP allowlist for the sandbox. For VPC peering we’ll need the CIDR and AWS account for the sandbox. Monica — can you include the peering details and a contact for infra ops?
3) Redaction: important for us — do you have examples of automated redaction rules you apply so we can map to our pipeline? Also need an audit-log sample showing token-level event entries.

We’re aligned on the high-level goals. One more ask: will the POC include a small canary of real traffic (~5% of a background job) or is it simulated only? If we can get a canary, we’ll observe live latency characteristics.

I’m looping in our infra lead in a follow-up (she’s OOO today) but we can return with the dataset link and peering preference by EOD tomorrow.

-David
David Chen
Staff Engineer, Integrations | Vectra Health
dchen@vectrahealth.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Discovery recap & POC charter (Vectra Health)

Hi David — quick infra note and the sandbox setup plan so your team can evaluate options.

Sandbox options (choose one)
- VPC peering (preferred): we provide AWS account: 987654321000 and CIDR 10.32.0.0/16. We'll need a one-time peering request and a route table entry for 10.32.0.0/16 -> peered VPC. Peering timeframe: ~1 business day once request is accepted.
- IP allowlist: provide a static public IP range; we’ll bind it to the sandbox load balancer. Faster but less secure.

Credentials / onboarding checklist (what Redwood will provide)
1) Temporary sandbox API key (valid 14 days) — attached as a stub: sandbox-credentials-stub.txt
2) IAM role to read from your S3 sample bucket (we’ll need the bucket ARN and a read-only path).
3) A baseline config for the model variant we plan to run (quantized small variant + full-precision baseline).
4) Audit log sample and a template for the retention/audit policy.

Security / compliance notes
- We will enable request-level audit logging and optional token redaction before logs are persisted. If you have formal retention limits, share those and we’ll configure the sink accordingly.

Next steps
- Karthik: confirm whether Vectra prefers peering or allowlist.
- David / Alexandra: share dataset link (CSV or NDJSON) and example redaction rules by EOD 8/25.
- I’ll provision the sandbox once we have the dataset and peering choice; baseline run expected within 24–36 hours of provisioning.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
